---
title: "Keep agents off each other's files with reservations"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Keep agents off each other's files with reservations}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---



A reservation is an advisory lease on a resource, held by one session for a
bounded time. Two agents editing one tree can use reservations to split it
between them. Pi's `edit` and `write` tools check them before every call.

## Take a reservation


``` bash
node tools/pi-coordination-endpoint.ts \
  "$STATE/coordination.url" "$STATE/coordination.duckdb" > "$STATE/endpoint.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$STATE/endpoint.pid"
until [ -s "$STATE/coordination.url" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
```

File resources are canonical `file:///` URIs. A reservation covers the
directory it names and everything below it. `docs-writer` reserves the
scratch directory for five minutes. This guide prints URIs relative to the
checkout:


``` r
url <- guide_url()
repo <- paste0("file://", normalizePath("."))
relative <- function(text) {
  gsub(repo, ".", gsub(paste0(repo, "/"), "", text, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
}
uri <- function(path) paste0(repo, "/", path)

writer <- register("docs-writer", ttl_ms = 300000)
held <- rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = writer$registration_id,
  resource = uri(".guide-scratch"),
  operation_key = "scratch", ttl_ms = 300000
))
held$resource <- relative(held$resource)
show(held, c("resource", "fencing_value", "replayed", "renewed"))
#> {
#>   "resource": ".guide-scratch",
#>   "fencing_value": 1,
#>   "replayed": false,
#>   "renewed": false
#> }
```

## A Pi agent is refused



A live Pi session, agent `editor`, is asked to write a file inside the
reserved directory:

``` sh
'pi' --provider 'openai-codex' --model 'gpt-6-astra' --no-extensions --thinking 'medium' -e './extensions/pi-ducknng/index.ts' --no-session -p \
  "$(printf %s \
    'You are agent `editor`. Use the write tool to create ' \
    '`.guide-scratch/notes.md` containing one line, `draft`. ' \
    'If the write is refused, do not retry it and do not ' \
    'write the file any other way. Call coordination_agents ' \
    'to see which agent holds the reservation. Report the ' \
    'refusal reason and the holder, beginning with ' \
    '`AGENT_EDIT_BLOCKED` only when the write was refused ' \
    'because another agent reserved the path.')"
```

> AGENT_EDIT_BLOCKED: Write refused because `.guide-scratch/notes.md` is covered by the `.guide-scratch` reservation held by `docs-writer`. No retry or alternative write attempted.

The adapter refused the tool call before it ran, so the file does not exist:


``` r
file.exists(".guide-scratch/notes.md")
#> [1] FALSE
```

The check covers Pi's `edit` and `write` tools. A command run through `bash`
is not checked, so reservations coordinate agents that cooperate. They do
not confine one that does not.

## What conflicts

A file reservation conflicts with the same path, with any path below it,
and with any directory above it. Paths are compared by segment, so a
sibling whose name merely starts the same way is free:


``` r
tester <- register("tester", ttl_ms = 300000)
try_reserve <- function(who, resource, key = resource) {
  reply <- tryCatch(
    rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
      registration_id = who$registration_id, resource = resource, operation_key = key
    )),
    error = function(error) error
  )
  if (inherits(reply, "error")) relative(failure(stop(reply))) else "reserved"
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  resource = c(".guide-scratch/data/raw.csv", ".", ".guide-scratchpad"),
  result = c(
    try_reserve(tester, uri(".guide-scratch/data/raw.csv")),
    try_reserve(tester, repo),
    try_reserve(tester, uri(".guide-scratchpad"))
  )
))
```



|resource                    |result                                                                           |
|:---------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|.guide-scratch/data/raw.csv |resource_conflict: .guide-scratch is reserved by docs-writer until 1790027378680 |
|.                           |resource_conflict: .guide-scratch is reserved by docs-writer until 1790027378680 |
|.guide-scratchpad           |reserved                                                                         |



The time in the refusal is when the lease ends, in Unix milliseconds.

`resource:` identifiers name things that are not files, such as a database
migration or a deploy slot. They conflict only when they are equal, so
`resource:db` and `resource:db/migrations` are two different resources:


``` r
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  caller = c("tester", "docs-writer", "docs-writer"),
  resource = c("resource:db/migrations", "resource:db/migrations", "resource:db"),
  result = c(
    try_reserve(tester, "resource:db/migrations"),
    try_reserve(writer, "resource:db/migrations"),
    try_reserve(writer, "resource:db")
  )
))
```



|caller      |resource               |result                                                                              |
|:-----------|:----------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|tester      |resource:db/migrations |reserved                                                                            |
|docs-writer |resource:db/migrations |resource_conflict: resource:db/migrations is reserved by tester until 1790027120969 |
|docs-writer |resource:db            |reserved                                                                            |



## Renewal, replay, and release

A holder renews by presenting its `lease_id`. Retrying the original
acquisition with the same `operation_key` returns the same lease instead of
a second one:


``` r
renewed <- rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = writer$registration_id, resource = uri(".guide-scratch"),
  lease_id = held$lease_id, ttl_ms = 300000
))
replayed <- rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = writer$registration_id, resource = uri(".guide-scratch"),
  operation_key = "scratch"
))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  call = c("renew", "replay"),
  same_lease = c(renewed$lease_id, replayed$lease_id) == held$lease_id,
  fencing_value = c(renewed$fencing_value, replayed$fencing_value),
  renewed = c(renewed$renewed, replayed$renewed),
  replayed = c(renewed$replayed, replayed$replayed)
))
```



|call   |same_lease | fencing_value|renewed |replayed |
|:------|:----------|-------------:|:-------|:--------|
|renew  |TRUE       |             1|TRUE    |FALSE    |
|replay |TRUE       |             1|FALSE   |TRUE     |



Only the instance that holds a lease can renew or release it:


``` r
failure(rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = tester$registration_id, resource = uri(".guide-scratch"),
  lease_id = held$lease_id
)))
#> [1] "lease_invalid: reservation lease is missing, expired, or stale"
```

Release is idempotent. Once it is released, the next holder receives a
larger fencing value:


``` r
released <- rpc_call(url, "release", list(
  registration_id = writer$registration_id, lease_id = held$lease_id))
again <- rpc_call(url, "release", list(
  registration_id = writer$registration_id, lease_id = held$lease_id))
next_holder <- rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = tester$registration_id, resource = uri(".guide-scratch/data"),
  operation_key = "data"
))
show(list(
  released = released$released, released_again = again$replayed,
  first_fencing_value = held$fencing_value, next_fencing_value = next_holder$fencing_value
))
#> {
#>   "released": true,
#>   "released_again": true,
#>   "first_fencing_value": 1,
#>   "next_fencing_value": 5
#> }
```

Fencing values increase across the whole project. A store that remembers the
largest value it has accepted can refuse a write from a holder whose lease
already passed to someone else, even one that paused through its whole TTL.

## Expiry

A lease ends at its TTL even if its holder never releases it. Unregistering
does not end it early, so a holder that leaves without releasing blocks the
resource until then. The shortest TTL is five seconds:


``` r
deployer <- register("deployer")
brief <- rpc_call(url, "reserve", list(
  registration_id = deployer$registration_id, resource = "resource:deploy",
  operation_key = "deploy", ttl_ms = 5000
))
invisible(rpc_call(url, "unregister", list(registration_id = deployer$registration_id)))
before <- try_reserve(writer, "resource:deploy", "deploy-now")
Sys.sleep(5.5)
after <- try_reserve(writer, "resource:deploy", "deploy-later")
c(before = before, after = after)
#>                                                                           before
#> "resource_conflict: resource:deploy is reserved by deployer until 1790027096242"
#>                                                                            after
#>                                                                       "reserved"
```

What each agent holds is one call away:


``` r
active <- rpc_call(url, "list_reservations", list(registration_id = writer$registration_id))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  resource = relative(vapply(active$reservations, `[[`, "", "resource")),
  owner = vapply(active$reservations, `[[`, "", "owner_agent_id"),
  fencing_value = vapply(active$reservations, `[[`, 0, "fencing_value"),
  mine = vapply(active$reservations, `[[`, TRUE, "owned_by_caller")
))
```



|resource               |owner       | fencing_value|mine  |
|:----------------------|:-----------|-------------:|:-----|
|.guide-scratch/data    |tester      |             5|FALSE |
|.guide-scratchpad      |tester      |             2|FALSE |
|resource:db            |docs-writer |             4|TRUE  |
|resource:db/migrations |tester      |             3|FALSE |
|resource:deploy        |docs-writer |             7|TRUE  |







> GUIDE_RESERVATIONS_VERIFIED: the gate refused a live agent, conflicts followed the path tree, and fencing values increased
